## Why This Is Asked
Tests low-level bit manipulation skills without branches, common in performance-critical code. It demonstrates proper masking, shifting, and word size preservation.

## Key Concepts
- Bit masking with 0x5555 (even positions) and 0xAAAA (odd positions)
- Left/right shifts combined with OR operation
- Branch-free operations on fixed-width integers

## Code Example
```c
uint16_t swapAdjacentBits16(uint16_t x) {
  return ((x & 0x5555) << 1) | ((x & 0xAAAA) >> 1);
}
```

## Examples
- Input: `0b10110011` (179) → Output: `0b01101101` (109)
- Input: `0b11110000` (240) → Output: `0b11110000` (240)

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to decompose a 128-bit value into fixed lanes and reconstruct a rotated layout using only bitwise ops and masking, without branches.

## Key Concepts
- Lane extraction with masks, 32-bit blocks
- Fixed-layout reconstruction; endianness awareness


- How to ensure correctness on little- vs big-endian targets?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Assesses ability to manipulate a 128-bit value using two 64-bit parts and leverage available intrinsics for performance. It tests understanding of bit significance ordering and boundary cases (zero input).

## Key Concepts

- 128-bit represented as two 64-bit words (lo then hi) and how trailing zeros map across the boundary
- Using 64-bit ctz intrinsics to build a 128-bit result in constant time
- Correct handling of the all-zero input returning 128

## Code Example

```c
int trailingZeroCount128(uint128 x) {
  if (x.lo != 0) return __builtin_ctzll(x.lo);
  if (x.hi != 0) return 64 + __builtin_ctzll(x.hi);
  return 128;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you implement this without compiler intrinsics?
- How would you port the approach to a 256-bit representation?

## Why This Is Asked

- Bitwise rotation semantics (wraps around word).
- Safe shifts with modulo-64 trick: ((0 - s) & 63).
- Branchless implementation for predictable performance.

```javascript
uint64_t rotateLeft64(uint64_t n, unsigned int k) {

}
```

## Why This Is Asked

This tests precise bit-twiddling with non-trivial masks and no loops, a common optimization pattern.

## Key Concepts

- Mask construction for adjacent-bit swaps
- Two-shift strategy and one return
- Edge cases: 64-bit boundaries, unsigned masking

## Code Example

```c
uint64_t swapAdjacent64(uint64_t n) {
  const uint64_t E = 0x5555555555555555ULL;
  const uint64_t O = 0xAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAULL;
  return ((n & E) << 1) | ((n & O) >> 1);
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you generalize to swap every 3-bit group? 
- What are the performance implications on modern CPUs?
